entries.name: The Amauna tribe
entries.content:
The Amauna tribe is located on a lost island somewhere in South America. They are a matriarchal and hierarchical society. The older women are the most prestigious in the tribe, and the tribe is led by 4 elders.

The women are kept ignorant about sexuality until they come of age and marry a man of the tribe. At that time the elders are in charge of giving them the necessary sexual education.

The 4 elders divide the responsibilities of the tribe:

Elder Inari (wise hunter): elder Inari is in charge of teaching the women the values of hunting, as well as thanking the jungle for prey with a prayer.

The old woman Kana (wild water): the old woman Kana is in charge of teaching the women the values and disciplines of fishing, as well as knowing which fish should be caught and which should be returned to the water. 

The old woman wila (powerful moon): the old woman wila is in charge of teaching the men and women of the village the values of construction.

Elder Maka (Daughter of the forest): elder Maka is in charge of teaching the men and women of the tribe the values of harvesting.

In the Amauna tribe the men have a value as men of the house, they are in charge of gathering fruits from the forest, taking care of the children and elders, and the construction of huts and different buildings of the tribe. Meanwhile the women are the warriors, hunters, fishermen, leaders and explorers of the tribe.

The Amauna tribe is only in charge of hunting and fishing so they do not know the values of planting food and are monogamous.
